title: Message Mesh — proto jot
content:
Quick pitch:
- Build a composable "message mesh" abstraction for per-request message transformations, routing and QoS policies before hitting the inference runtime. Think of it as a tiny, in-process pipeline designer that sits between API layer and model dispatcher.

Why?
- Many feature teams end up reimplementing the same routing/transform/fallback logic in different places (session stitching, persona injection, compression heuristics, cache layers).
- Centralizing primitives reduces duplication, speeds experiments, and keeps SLOs consistent.
- Gives product teams a low-friction way to try response-tiering, multi-model fanout, and policy-based fallbacks without changing model clients.

Core ideas (high level):
- Message building blocks: transform, annotate, route, sample, splice, fallback. Each block is tiny and composable.
- Runtime: pipeline description (JSON/YAML) attached to API key/route; evaluated per request. Fast, single-threaded execution; deterministic.
- Hooks: pre-call hooks (e.g., prefix injection, conversation stitching), post-call hooks (reranks, filter), and sidecar actions (audit log, telemetry emit).
- Policy layer: QoS tags (low/med/high), cost budget, fallback chain (quantized smaller model -> cached snippet -> truncated response).

Rough user stories (product-focused):
- As a product engineer, I can declare a pipeline for route /assistant/compact that injects a persona and compresses history using model X and routes to model Y for generation.
  - Acceptance: pipeline deployed via console or API, p50 latency increase <= 15% vs baseline, and end-to-end correctness verified on smoke prompt set.

- As an SRE, I can attach a cost cap per route that enacts automatic downgrades to cheaper model variants when budget is hit.
  - Acceptance: simulated traffic triggers downgrade; logs show decision and fallback used.

- As an ML engineer, I can run A/B where pipeline variant A does reranking with model R and variant B uses heuristic score; we collect quality metrics and can rollback.
  - Acceptance: rollouts visible in Console (per-model/per-pipeline metrics) and easy to revert.

Acceptance criteria for v0 (internal alpha):
- Pipeline DSL MVP (JSON) with 6 blocks implemented: inject, compress, cache-lookup, route, call-model, fallback.
- API to attach pipeline to route or api-key scope.
- Canary rollout to <10 internal customers; telemetry for p50/p95 latency, cost delta, and correctness (eval prompt set).
- End-to-end tests + a minimal example app in repo.

Design notes / naive sketches:
- DSL example:
  {
    "pipeline": [
      {"inject": {"template": "You are a helpful assistant."}},
      {"compress": {"strategy": "summary", "model": "tiny-summarizer"}},
      {"cache_lookup": {"key": "conversation_shard_v1"}},
      {"route": {"by": "qos", "map": {"high": "redwood-llama-13b", "low": "redwood-llama-7b-q4"}}},
      {"call_model": {"model_param_overrides": {"max_tokens": 256}}},
      {"fallback": {"steps": ["use_cached", "use-7b-quant" ]}}
    ]
  }

- Execution: pipeline executed inline before model dispatch; lightweight state object passes through. No separate infra tier (v0), keep within API worker to avoid extra hop.

Experiments to run first:
- Compression vs eviction: is cheap summarizer + context window increase cheaper than long context? A/B with cost per 1k tokens + user quality score.
- Fallback chaining latency: measure time and availability when falling back to quantized model vs return partial response.
- Cost cap behavior: how often do we downgrade under realistic traffic mixes (chatty vs transactional).

Metrics to capture (minimum):
- p50/p95 request latency (with and without pipeline)
- delta cost per 1k tokens for route
- feature adoption: # pipelines created / active routes
- quality regressions on eval set (BLEU/ROUGE or human rubric)

Operational concerns / risks:
- Complexity explosion: too many blocks combinatorially => hard to reason about SLOs. Need sane defaults + limits per pipeline.
- Security: pipeline templates could inject unsafe instructions — enforce tenant scoping and validation.
- Observability: need per-block traces and attribution.
- Performance: doing compress and rerank in API worker may increase p95; consider offloading later.

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- Alpha (internal): lightweight API, 6 blocks, console editor disabled (API only), <10 internal teams. 2 weeks.
- Beta (selected customers): add console editor with templating, telemetry dashboards, 3 customer integrations, 4–6 weeks.
- GA: hardened validation, quotas, canary controls, docs and sample templates. 2+ months.

Open questions (TODOs):
- DSL format: JSON vs compact YAML vs UI graph. JSON easiest for now.
- How to represent stateful vs stateless blocks (e.g., cache writes between requests)?
- Permissions model: who can upload pipelines for a tenant? route-level vs api-key-level?
- Fallback semantics: synchronous fallback chain vs async fallback + partial response.

Next immediate steps (for me):
- Spike: implement minimal pipeline runner in API worker (2 days) — prototype repo in message-mesh-proto.
- Quick eval harness: 50 prompts, simulate 1k req/day, measure cost/latency delta (3 days).
- Sync: 30m with Maya + Kai to prioritize blocks and risk limits.

Notes to self / scratches:
- Keep block primitives orthogonal and small. Resist the urge to add too many transform types early.
- Consider naming it "message mesh" vs "pipeline"; mesh evokes routing which is useful for multi-model fanout.
- Use existing cache key conventions (see stash spec).
- Revisit with infra: if p95 grows > 2x, need to consider sidecar approach or background precompute.

Random links/refs to copy into ticket later:
- linear:INF-7123 (proto + experiment)
- GH: redwood-inference/message-mesh-proto PR#12 (basic runner)
- convo-primer templates: /confluence/Message Mesh sketch

End of jot.
